text: Yeah, well, when I think about even just the last year alone in terms of the tokenized security space and RWAs in general, the space has more than doubled in size. And if you look within that, you'll see that areas like tokenized Treasuries have grown probably now over 800% in the same time period. And so one of the things that I think we're really focused on at Securitize is ensuring that when we are going to bring investments on chain, we're going to unlock or find some additional benefits for both the asset issuers like Nick mentioned, Apollo, VanEck, BlackRock, even Hamilton Lane, as well as for the end investor itself. A lot of the investors that are coming on chain today to buy products like these, these are investors that for the most part already in the digital asset ecosystem. They're already folks that may have, you know, speculated on assets like Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and they're looking for diversification with top tier asset issuers and often with cash flowing investments. But if you compare the attributes that these products have in an on chain environment to their traditional counterparts, we hold ourselves accountable and responsible to give them some other features. So for example, in Solana as well as other chains, our BlackRock tokenized treasury fund, the dividends are paid out on a daily basis to investors as opposed to, you know, in an traditional Rails environment, those dividends get paid monthly, quarterly, etc. So when you think about the compounding effects that that has for the end investor, when you think about their immediate access to the capital, these are objectively attributes and features that investors are now looking for and are really starting to demand out of their on chain investments. I think when you also think about not just the investments themselves, but the other opportunities that exist for them because they're on chain, we're starting to see a lot of interoperability, not just cross chain working with partners like Wormhole, but also being able to bring these investments into the DEFI ecosystem. So largely these pools of capital and these types of investments have never really had the opportunity in a traditional format to exist with lending and borrowing and all the great things that investors can do in Defi. But now with the advent of folks like Kamino and Drift and the Solana ecosystem, if you are minting these assets on chain, you, you're often able to now bring them into the DEFI ecosystem to either leverage the assets further or come up with other strategies that ultimately enhance the yields for investors. And a lot of that demand is really what's driving the growth of the space in general.

text: Saeed, how does Wormhole facilitate a lot of this growth? And then on a higher level, what's your relationship with Solana and how do you guys really try to work together?
speaker: A

text: I think a lot of it has to do with giving the end user or the asset issuer the ability to make the trade offs that they want to make. So you kind of want to have an extremely flexible stack that if an asset issuer wants to be native on Solana, like blackrock for instance, they can do that, but they don't have to sacrifice their growth. So if there are other trade offs that users or institutions are making and they want to be on other chains, that can happen without having a complex amount of work and operational overhead to be able to manage the asset. So it can be native on both chains, it can communicate with each other. You have all of that infrastructure set. So if at any point a securitized user who has BlackRock on one chain, like the Bittle token on one chain, and wants to move it to another, they can do that in a purely native fashion. And I think that's been something that we've helped with a lot of institutions support. And it's particularly important when you start to talk about payments and you start to talk about stablecoin issuers and you and intrinsic to the work that they're doing is that we want this to proliferate. We don't know where the merchants are going to be, we don't know where the asset issuers are going to be, and we don't know what the payments networks are going to allow. But what we do know is that we don't want any limitations in terms of a blockchain, in terms of the type of assets stored, in terms of the type of wrapping of that asset, all of that needs to be abstracted away. And that's a lot of the work that we've done. And I think we've had a decent amount of success attracting some of the biggest names in the world to start using those rails and start issuing their assets across multiple chains.
speaker: B

text: Michael, I think one of the real buzz phrases right now is we want to tokenize everything and everything and their mother needs to be tokenized. But I don't think we always think that that's the case. Right. So what are some of the misnomers around tokenization or some of the myths that you're seeing out there?
speaker: A

text: Yeah, I mean, I think one of the biggest ones that we're having to battle at the moment is that there's this inherent belief that if you tokenize something, it immediately makes the asset itself more liquid. That's just simply not true. Liquidity and the ability for an asset to be bought and sold or there to be price discovery or a marketplace, the same dynamics exist for it in a traditional rail environment or in an on chain environment. So simply tokenizing something does not inherently make it more liquid. What I would say in terms of what we're doing at Securitize and the types of opportunities that we're seeing from asset issuers trying to satisfy the demand that the on chain investor is looking for really surrounds investments that are highly liquid and more than anything are assets that, that again have the most frequent ability to be bought and sold, redeemed, purchased, but also cash flowing. And so that's why I think we've seen the growth we have around both tokenized Treasuries. You've seen the growth around now private credit. And what will be exciting for us as we kind of enter into the back part of this year is the demand is starting to shift both in terms of the product structure itself, like what type of product wrapper is moving into the tokenized format as well as what the underlying exposures are. So one of the projects I know we're proud of is we tokenized Exodus Public company traded on the New York Stock Exchange. So there's obviously a lot of buzz now around being able to tokenize equities, ETFs, etc. And as more investors come into the on chain environment, you're going to see a broader spectrum of product exposures and product wrappers.
speaker: C

text: Yeah, I think there's a tremendous amount of talent in the city and in this country and I think a lot of it has had to move elsewhere because of a lot of stuff that's happened in the past. I think a lot of the excitement and acceleration and why you want to continue to invest here is really around the new administrative changes and their views around stablecoins, their views around crypto, their views around regulation and Bring clarity. I mean, it seems like the administration has a view that there's an insane or an immense untapped demand for digital dollars. And they think that that is core to their strategy for, you know, addressing inflation, addressing some of the major economic forces that, that, that, that kind of concern the government, concern the Fed, concern the Treasury. And so when you see the Treasury Secretary out there really pushing stablecoin adoption, you see the Senate passing the Genius Act, I don't think it's happening in a vacuum. And I don't think it's just because, like, oh, we just decided we like stablecoins. I think there's like a very, very intelligent strategy in terms of. We've seen things like Tether, who really have a very niche market in terms of servicing, like crypto traders on exchanges mainly, and a little bit of payments in certain geographical locations, you know, because become a top 10 buyer of US treasuries in a very short amount of time with very little support. And I think that's a very, very powerful signal for regulators and lawmakers in this country and business people in this country that there is an insane untapped amount of demand for these digital dollars. And so we should just open the door wide open, set some very clear guidelines, some rules of the road. If you want to launch a stablecoin, you can do it. You can do it right here in America, and you can go and try to service that demand wherever it is around the world. And in order for you to actually do that, you need to have trustless systems that are based on decentralization. You need to have instant settlement, you need to actually provide a better product, and you need to provide transparency, and you need to open up the market to the entire world to interact with it. I think if you look at this past week, we had a Treasury auction that was very interesting. A lot of eyebrows were raised. So, yeah, I would say when you see those two things coupled together, it gives you a strong sense of a trend of a signal, and it's worth investing in. And I think there's a lot of talent in the city and in this country that sees the same thing and is starting to build products and infrastructure that can support that.

text: And actually, just when you talk about transparency, I think that's a really important theme because investors are looking for that transparency.
